headline: DeepSeek open-sources inference optimizations with 60–85% faster generation
summary: DeepSeek has released new inference optimizations that significantly boost generation speed by 60-85%. This open-source contribution aims to enhance the performance of large language models.
details: DeepSeek has open-sourced significant inference optimizations, promising a 60-85% speed increase for AI model generation. This release, part of their DeepSpec project, focuses on enhancing the efficiency of large language models (LLMs).

DeepSpec is described as a full-stack codebase for training and evaluating speculative decoding algorithms. Speculative decoding allows models to generate text faster by predicting future tokens and then verifying them in parallel, drastically reducing latency.

By making these advanced algorithms and codebase publicly available, DeepSeek aims to accelerate research and development in the AI community. This move could lead to more efficient and responsive AI applications across various industries.

The optimizations are detailed in a comprehensive PDF, providing technical insights into their implementation and performance benchmarks. This transparency fosters collaboration and allows developers to integrate these improvements into their own projects.

headline_marked: [[Windows 11 runs on DDR1-era hardware]] with Core 2 Q6600 and ATI Radeon HD 4650 AGP
headline: Windows 11 runs on DDR1-era hardware with Core 2 Q6600 and ATI Radeon HD 4650 AGP
summary: A tech enthusiast successfully installed and ran Windows 11 on a system featuring DDR1 RAM, a Core 2 Quad Q6600, and an ATI Radeon HD 4650 AGP card. The system is reported to be "completely stable."
details: Inspired by a 'RAMpocalypse' affecting older memory supplies, an enthusiast named Omores successfully installed and ran Windows 11 on a system built with DDR1 RAM, a Core 2 Quad Q6600 CPU, and an ATI Radeon HD 4650 AGP graphics card. Despite the vintage components, Omores claims the system is "completely stable."

DDR1 memory, which replaced SDR SDRAM, first became available around the turn of the century, with initial data rates like DDR-200 and DDR-266. The system utilized an ASRock ConRoe 865PE motherboard, a legendary board known for bridging generations by allowing Core 2 Duo/Quad chips with DDR1 RAM and AGP graphics.

The ATI Radeon HD 4650 AGP card required significant effort to integrate with Windows 11. Omores managed to get AGP 8X fully functional and H.264 hardware decoding active by "hacking" in ATI's Windows 7 64-bit drivers from 2012.

After confirming the setup with tools like CPU-Z and GPU-Z, Omores demonstrated the Windows 11 system running modern browsers, embedded video with hardware decoding, and a handful of games and 3D benchmarks without glitches. Notably, the system was even shown running Crysis.

Omores later elaborated on the driver installation process on Reddit, noting that Windows 11 is "rock stable on these older systems with no UEFI whatsoever and only ACPI 1.1." He added that Windows 11 IoT officially supports BIOS systems, which helps explain the smooth operation.
